scope: Full HTTP/1.1 request parse, route dispatch through a 1002-route table, body decode or decrypt, schema validation, controller action, response validation, and response encode or encrypt
target: DigitalOcean s-1vcpu-512mb-10gb: 1 vCPU, 512 MB advertised, 10 GB disk, $4/month at test time
load_generator: DigitalOcean c-4: 4 dedicated vCPUs and 8 GB memory

method.scenario_order: Rotated by repetition; all raw runs retained

json_decode_only.description: Generic JSON parse and acknowledgement response without schema enforcement

validated_json.description: JSON decode, eight-field schema validation, typed controller input, response-schema validation, and JSON response

validated_cbor.description: Bounded deterministic CBOR decode, the same schema and controller work, response-schema validation, and deterministic CBOR response

validated_cose.description: COSE Encrypt0 authentication/decryption, CBOR decode, the same schema and controller work, response validation, CBOR encode, and fresh-nonce COSE encryption

qualifiers: This is a synthetic in-memory acknowledgement endpoint. It does not include a database, external services, TLS, HTML rendering, logging middleware, or public-internet latency.
The COSE scenario performs authenticated encryption in both directions. It is not comparable to a benchmark that only serializes CBOR or only encrypts the response.
The generic JSON baseline verifies decode and field use but intentionally does not enforce the schema. The validated JSON delta is the release-relevant schema cost for this payload and endpoint.
Absolute throughput varied during the run. The report uses medians and publishes every raw result rather than deleting slower observations.

The release candidate still needs the separately validated optimized-router integration before an absolute final-release headline is published. Relative schema and codec comparisons used the same router and route table.
